title: control-evidence-journalizer-and-geofenced-retention-scheduler
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Objective: Build a reusable 'Journalizer' service that maps SOC 2 / ISO 27001 control assertions to concrete artifacts, collects and normalizes telemetry across jurisdictions, and automatically composes auditor-facing evidence bundles with geofenced retention enforcement. Scope includes mapping control IDs to collectors (audit log, API request traces, console events, KMS access), retention rules by region, and an export/playbook for SOC2/ISO auditors.

Background: Customers need reproducible evidence for control assertions while complying with regional data residency and retention policies. Existing work (PM-30399, ENG-76133) has prototypes for log collection and snapshotting, but artifacts are scattered and lack standardized mapping and retention enforcement. This ticket unifies the mapping layer, orchestration for evidence composition, and a scheduler that applies region-specific retention windows and redaction rules.

Goals / Success Criteria:
- A canonical control->artifact mapping registry (CSV/JSON) that links SOC2/ISO control IDs to required artifact types and retention classes.
- Implementation of Journalizer service that can ingest collectors' outputs and emit standardized evidence entries (signed, checksummed, timestamped).
- Geofenced Retention Scheduler that enforces retention periods and supports legal hold, purge, and archive paths per jurisdiction.
- Exportable auditor bundles (ZIP + signed manifest) with machine-readable index and human summary.
- End-to-end e2e runbook and automated smoke tests proving bundle reproducibility.

Scope exclusions: deep proof-of-custody cryptographic ledger (out of scope for initial delivery), long-term cold archival UI (catalog only), and custom per-customer attestation flows (handled in later phase).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Registry created and populated for at least SOC2 CC7, CC6 and ISO A.8/A.12 mappings. 2) Journalizer ingests sample collectors (audit-log, api-trace, console-events, kms-access) and produces normalized evidence entries for 95% of sample cases. 3) Retention Scheduler enforces per-region retention windows and honors legal-hold flag during purge runs. 4) Auditor bundle can be generated via API and validates against manifest checksum and signature. 5) Security review completed and approved. 6) Demo with sample customer showing automated bundle generation in staging.

risks_and_tradeoffs: - Precompute vs on-demand: precomputing evidence bundles reduces auditor latency but increases storage and cost; we'll support on-demand generation first and consider scheduled precompute for high-touch customers. - Granular redaction: aggressive redaction to minimize PII in bundles can remove useful audit context; propose configurable redaction templates per control. - Cross-region joins: collecting artifacts that touch multiple regions requires careful custody tagging; we will include custody metadata in entries and mark cross-border items for manual review. - Cost: normalized artifacts and signing adds storage and CPU; initial rollout limited to 'premium' customers to control cost exposure.
